invariants.note: THE ROUND'S RESULT IS ABOUT THE FACTORY, NOT THE PRODUCT. R6.1 and a concurrent R7 Embodiment round both wrote this tree, both branching from INV-R6, and the R6.1 receipt then claimed one parent and one operation over a state containing two. It disclosed the ambiguity honestly and that was not enough: a transition receipt exists to identify an exact parent, an exact operation and an exact successor, and one that cannot do that is byte-consistent with a history that did not happen. GPT-5.6 also reproduced the mechanical half — `mosaic/operations.json` was introduced by the concurrent round, entered no manifest, and could be edited on a copy of the finished artifact with the gate still passing. SECOND RESULT, and it is the one I got wrong on my own account: R6.1 measured that `active_unresolved` and `strict` agree on every real record and I declined to build a distinguishing case, calling it manufacturing a witness. That conflated a positive control with evidence. A control asks whether the implementation distinguishes what it claims to; it says nothing about production records. §5b2 now proves the readings differ on a terminated-only framework, and ASR-TERMINATOR-UNOBSERVABLE remains the separate measurement that no real record does. Both are true and the artifact carries both.

transition.operation: factory-integrity round. No theorem changed and no claim was retyped. What changed is what the artifact can say about its own transitions.
